title: picomatch is patched against single-branch repeated extglob ReDoS (GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf): '+(*)' answers a long non-match at once, ordinary globs match as before
steps: S1: In the TCH checkout after pnpm install, run run.cmd (no database, no network).
S2: Confirm every test named in run.tests reports ok.
expect: Every picomatch copy the root install holds (2.3.2 and 4.0.7) is the patched one.
picomatch('+(*)') and makeRe('+(*a)') answer a long non-matching input well under the test timeout; *.js, **/*.md, +(a|b), !(x) match as before.
Each EmDash theme carries the root patch files and names them in patchedDependencies.

A patch-only release cut from a published EmDash quickstart (scripts/emdash-patch-release.mjs) carries the same patches, a lockfile byte-identical to what pnpm writes for them, the new version everywhere the zip states it, and a distribution.json, manifest, SHA256SUMS and tracy_setting.json that verify.
fence: lib/parse.js change of micromatch/picomatch#246 applied via pnpm patchedDependencies in root and the six themes

tests: the root install has a patched copy of every picomatch version it holds
picomatch 2.3.2: single-branch repeated extglobs answer a long non-match quickly
picomatch 2.3.2: ordinary globs match as before
picomatch 4.0.7: single-branch repeated extglobs answer a long non-match quickly
picomatch 4.0.7: ordinary globs match as before
each EmDash theme carries the root patch files and names them in patchedDependencies
patchLockfile gives back, byte for byte, the lockfile pnpm wrote for the patches on every theme
the patch hash is the sha256 of the patch file, the one the develop lockfiles record
patchLockfile patches importer versions and refuses a lockfile that already has patches
the workspace block and the Dockerfile lines are the develop ones, put where #684 put them
cut: the new zip carries the patch and the version, verifies, and the release files name it
cut refuses what it cannot cut honestly
cut refuses a file it reads or carries that SHA256SUMS does not list, naming it
cut refuses a release whose aggregate status is not what its gates add up to, or whose receipt disagrees
cut refuses a release whose recorded gates did not pass, or whose two records disagree
cut checks the published kit and carries it with the new contract template-kit.json
notesFor reports a mention of the old version it does not know how to move
the same published release cuts the same bytes, whenever and wherever it is cut
